text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- South Korean President Kim Young Sam agrees to meet opposition parties to try to resolve industrial crisis sparked by new labour law.

- Japan will boost cooperation with Asian countries in tackling various problems, in addition to promoting trade liberalisation and other traditional areas of cooperation, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto says in parliament speech.
- Meeting with friends at playground turns into painful experience for sales assistant when someone throws sand-filled incense burner from ninth storey window, hitting her in head.
- Singapore's trade expected to grow between five and seven percent this year, benefiting from projected higher world trade growth and pick-up in global electronics demand in second half.
- Singapore electronics output records five year low of nine percent growth.
- Singapore shares surge, with key indices soaring to highest levels in several months, as institutional and retail players return to market with vengeance.
- Shares in Tri-M Technologies (S) rise as much as 19 percent on news two businessmen launch takeover bid for the contract manufacturer at US$1.10 per share.
- Singapore's key electronics sector expected to grow between 10 and 15 percent this year.
- Growth in non-oil domestic exports slows to 2.7 percent in 1996.
- Trading and manufacturing group Haw Par Brothers International and listed subsidiary Tiger Medicals reach amicable settlement over lawsuit filed in 1990.
- Shares of FHTK holdings end five percent above initial public offering price on company's main board trading debut.
- Jurong Cement enters two-tier provisional transaction deal with Nomura Trading Co of Japan.
